correctness.rationale: Under the fully specified uniform null and full radius range, ordered internal gaps alone determine the Čech Euler curve (by the nerve theorem for intervals and component counting). With m=n−1, its one-sided deviations at a jump are k−mp_k and k−1−mp_k. Between jumps the centering is monotone. This verifies the two rank-band inequalities and the 1/2 lower bound. In Step 1 read the undefined typographical ‘ν_k’ in A_k as the immediately defined upper bound u_k, as required by H_k=1−p_k^(1/n). Translation of the uniform full-spacing simplex gives the nth-power joint survivor; grouping boxes by counts gives the stated multinomial inclusion–exclusion. For z<1 the gap rank intervals are ordered, so the product formula holds while the top corner lies in the simplex. Strict midpoint concavity gives slack >2/(n+1) at z=1/2; at z=1 the first upper gap is 1, and another strictly positive upper gap exists if n≥3. Thus the unique crossing β_n exists. The affine density n!m!(1−∑h_k) integrates to the stated product and each width is asymptotic to its derivative times ε, giving the positive constant. The maximizing endpoint m is approached by clustered observations; continuity on the gap simplex and positive interior density give the full support. For n=2, p_1 is uniform and Z_2=max(p_1,1−p_1).
